newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mediator says airline talks going slowly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mediator says airline talks going slowly.

text.p: The federal mediator overseeing the contract talks between American Airlines and its pilots union said Wednesday the talks were going slowly and with increasing difficulty.

Kenneth Hipp, chairman of the National Mediation Board, after day-long meetings between American and the Allied Pilots Association, said the two sides met until late on Tuesday night and throughout Wednesday. "I would characterize the talks as going slowly with increasing difficulty," he said.
But Hipp said talks between labour and management often go slowly in the beginning and that a great deal can be put together in a short time.
The pilots from the nation's second largest airline are set to strike just after midnight Friday (0501 GMT Saturday) unless the two sides can reach an agreement.
The pilots Wednesday rejected a new pay offer from Fort Worth, Tex.-based American and a union spokesman said "there has been no progress so far" in the talks.

Meanwhile, President Clinton urged the sides to use the mediation process to resolve their dispute, which he said had huge implications for the country. A strike would disrupt travel plans for hundreds of thousands of people who take American's 2,200 flights worldwide each day.
